rounds.text: Savita Oil Technologies Ltd is supported by explosive fundamental acceleration, evidenced by a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 26% [E16] and a massive compounded profit growth of 222% over the same period [E19]. Operational efficiency is surging, with operating margins expanding to 11% in the TTM against 7% three years earlier [E27], and hitting 25% in the June 2026 quarter compared to just 6% in the year-ago quarter [E28]. The business is exceptionally well-funded with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E35], generating solid financial muscle including Rs 137 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 107 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E32, E33]. Institutional conviction is clearly strengthening, demonstrated by domestic institutions increasing their stake from 7.42% to 13.18% alongside positive institutional money flow [E41, E42], while benefiting from a strong sector tailwind score of +0.61 [E70]. Momentum is unmatched with a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E49] and a rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 [E62]. Conceded: [E43], [E44], [E61].

Savita Oil Technologies Ltd trades at an unfavorable valuation supported by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 667 per share against a market price of Rs 737, leaving a negative margin of safety of -10.5% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the company exhibits poor multi-year profitability trends, with compounded profit growth over 5 years at -9% and over 3 years at -13% [E17, E18], alongside a low median return on equity of 8% over the last 3 years and last year [E25, E26]. Momentum risks are also prominent as the stock sits 92% of the way up its 52-week range and is flagged for being extended, trading at 2.79 times its book value [E46, E60, E67]. Insider selling compounds these valuation and fundamental concerns, with promoter holding declining from 71.92% in Sep 2023 to 68.93% in Jun 2026, and foreign institutional holdings dropping from 1.73% to 1.02% over the same period [E39, E40]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing performance with a 12-month price return of 81.4%, an operating cash flow of Rs 137 Cr in Mar 2026, and positive domestic institutional buying [E32, E41, E50].
